The tech-heavy NASDAQ is down more than 2% in early hours.

Separately, the cryptocurrency corporation Binance says it has been expertly hacked.
Saboteurs have ripped off well over $6 billion from Binance.
It's possibly the most costly heist of a crypto company ever.
President Trump is changing his campaign plans,
and PR Sage Miller says he is altering his weekend travel.
He has canceled his in-person rallies in Iowa and Kansas this weekend.
Instead of traveling to those states, Trump is opting to host 19 telerallies,
perhaps more bang for his buck, rather than fitting in those two in-person rallies over the weekend.
And PR Sage Miller reporting.
A Russian drone attack killed at least 14 people in central Ukraine.
And PR's Juanica Kissis reports.
European leaders called Thursday's Russian attack on the main train station
in the city of Nipro "cruel and devastating."
Russia also attacked Ukraine's capital Kyiv with ballistic missiles.
The explosions were heard from NPR's bureau in Kyiv.
In his evening video address, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky
mourned those who were killed.
He brought up another attack in the northern city of Cherniv.
There was a strike right in the middle of the city, Zelensky said.
Two girls were killed, 15 years old, Yana and Maria.
Russian attacks only paused in the southern Herson region,
as part of a local ceasefire to aid a frontline town.
Joanna Kissis, NPR News, Kyiv.
An environmental advocacy group is urging the Supreme Court
to keep a temporary block on hundreds of miles of border wall construction in West Texas.
Carlos Morales reports.
The Center for Biological Diversity argues that if the construction is allowed to resume,
it would result in the "permanent alteration of an irreplaceable landscape."
The Trump administration's border security plan for the beloved big band region of Texas
has stirred up national attention and bipartisan backlash.
The lawsuit at issue argues that the federal government's plans are unconstitutional
and that the plaintiffs in the case would be irreparably harmed.
The federal government maintains the barriers are needed
and blasted the lower court order that halted construction as baseless and unprecedented.
You're listening to NPR.
Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado
has given her first press conference in Venezuela since returning from exile.
She is backing calls for national elections next year.
Machado, a Nobel Peace Prize winner, thanked President Trump for his support.
Acting Venezuelan leader Delsi Rodriguez dismissed Machado's comments as a "show."
Most Americans will turn their clocks back an hour this weekend,
and PR's Windsor-Johnson reports a new national poll
finds many would rather stop changing them altogether.
A new poll by the public research group YouGov finds 63 percent of Americans want to end the
twice-yearly clock changes, but there is disagreement over which time to keep.
42 percent favor permanent daylight saving time, which means more daylight in the evening,
compared with 28 percent who prefer standard time.
The debate over the issue continues in Congress,
where legislation has bounced between the House and Senate for years.
The Senate passed the Sunshine Protection Act in 2022, but it never advanced in the House.
A newer measure passed the House in July and remains stalled in the Senate amid
concerns over darker mornings during the winter months.
For now, though, clocks fall back an hour early on Sunday.
Windsor-Johnson, NPR News.
There is no school today in Milwaukee, Wisconsin.
The city is toasting this year's World Series winners, the Milwaukee Brewers, with a parade.
They took the series four games to one this week over the Tampa Bay Rays.
Milwaukee Public Schools says its schools and offices will be closed today
and is offering the Brewers congratulations.
It's NPR.
